But both poles have political connotations. Radical might relate to challenging authority (authority=1) and perhaps liberty (liberty=1) because radical often wants more freedom from constraints. Centrist may respect authority. I'd mark authority and liberty as 1. Also general? Possibly, but not clearly. Notes: radical vs centrist political orientation; radical challenges authority, centrist respects it.

352: monotone :: expressive - Not clearly related to any foundation. Expressive might relate to freedom of expression (liberty?) but weak. General? No. So all 0. Notes: Not clearly related to moral foundations.

353: love-focused :: money-focused - Could relate to care (love) vs fairness? Money might relate to fairness or cheating? But not strong. Possibly general moral goodness? Love is often seen as morally good, money-focused as greedy (vice). So general=1. Also care? Love-focused relates to care. So care=1, general=1. Notes: love-focused aligns with care; money-focused may be seen as morally questionable.

354: transparent :: machiavellian - Transparent is honest, machiavellian is manipulative. This relates to fairness (honesty) and deception. Also general morality. So fairness=1 (honesty), general=1. Notes: transparent implies honesty, machiavellian implies deceit.

370: junkie :: straight edge - Junkie implies addiction and vice, straight edge implies self-discipline and purity. So purity=1 (vice and virtue). Also general=1. Notes: junkie is impure vice, straight edge is pure virtue.

I'd mark authority=1 (dystopian has negative authority), liberty=1 (utopian has freedom), general=1 (moral evaluation of society). Notes: dystopian often features oppressive authority, utopian idealizes fairness and freedom.
